snapshot.exam_hook: 🏆 UPSC VICTORY HOOK: You are ready. The 100 days are in your blood. Stay calm. Be precise. Eliminate. Conquer.

quick_notes.title: Polity 10-Hooks
quick_notes.detail: Preamble, FR (14-32), DPSP, President (72/123), Parliament (Joint Sitting), Judiciary (Writs), Federalism (GST/FC), Local Government (73/74), Constitutional Bodies, Schedules.
quick_notes.explanation: The Preamble is the introduction to the Constitution of India that states its goals, such as justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity. Fundamental Rights (FR), found in Articles 14 to 32 of the Constitution, are basic human rights that the government cannot violate, like the right to equality and the right to constitutional remedies which allows you to go to a court. The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are instructions in the Constitution for the government to make laws for the welfare of the people, like providing free education, but they are not enforceable in court. The President of India has the power to grant pardons or reduce sentences under Article 72 and to make ordinances, which are temporary laws, under Article 123 when Parliament is not in session. In Parliament, a Joint Sitting is a combined meeting of both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha to resolve a disagreement on a bill. The Judiciary, meaning the courts, can issue five types of Writs, which are court orders like Habeas Corpus (to produce a detained person) or Mandamus (to order a public official to do their duty), to enforce Fundamental Rights. Federalism in India divides power between the central government and state governments, including the Goods and Services Tax (GST) which is a single tax on goods and services, and the Finance Commission (FC) which decides how tax money is shared between the centre and states. Local Government refers to village-level governance through Panchayats, covered by Article 73 of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, and city-level governance through Municipalities, covered by Article 74 of the 74th Constitutional Amendment. Constitutional Bodies are independent institutions created by the Constitution, such as the Election Commission of India which conducts elections. Schedules are lists in the Constitution that contain specific details, like Schedule 5 which deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas and Schedule 6 which deals with tribal areas in the northeast.

quick_notes.title: Economy 10-Hooks
quick_notes.detail: GDP/GNP/Real, Inflation (CPI/RBI), Monetary Policy (Repo), Budget (Deficits), Taxation (GST), Poverty (Tendulkar), Planning (NITI), External (BOP/FDI), Agriculture (MSP), Global Orgs (IMF).
quick_notes.explanation: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total money value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a year. Gross National Product (GNP) is GDP plus income earned by residents from abroad, minus income earned by foreigners within the country. Real GDP adjusts the nominal GDP for inflation, which is a general rise in prices. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures the average change in prices paid by urban consumers for a basket of goods and services, and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) uses it to guide monetary policy, which controls the money supply and interest rates. The Repo Rate is the interest rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks, and changing it is a key tool of monetary policy. A government budget has deficits: a revenue deficit means the government's current income (like taxes) is less than its daily expenses, and a fiscal deficit is the total borrowing needed when all spending exceeds all income except borrowings. The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a single, nationwide indirect tax on the supply of goods and services, replacing many older taxes. The Tendulkar Committee defined poverty based on spending on food, education, and health to set a poverty line. The NITI Aayog replaced the old Planning Commission and now helps the central government design and implement development plans with states. The Balance of Payments (BOP) records all economic transactions between India and the rest of the world, while Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is when a company from one country makes a physical investment (like building a factory) in another country. The Minimum Support Price (MSP) is a guaranteed price the government promises to pay farmers for certain crops, to protect them from price falls. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is a global organization that provides loans and advice to countries facing economic problems.

quick_notes.title: S&T + Env 10-Hooks
quick_notes.detail: ISRO (Launchers), Biotech (CRISPR), AI/Blockchain, Nuclear (3-stages), Nano, Ecosystem (Energy flow), Biodiversity (Hotspots), Climate (Paris/Montreal), Pollution (BOD), WPA 1972.
quick_notes.explanation: S&T and Environment 10-Hooks ISRO, which stands for the Indian Space Research Organisation, builds and launches rockets called launchers to put satellites into space. In biotechnology, CRISPR is a precise gene-editing tool that acts like molecular scissors to cut and change DNA in living organisms. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is computer systems that can learn and make decisions, while Blockchain is a secure digital ledger that records transactions across many computers. India's nuclear power program follows a three-stage plan: first using natural uranium, then plutonium, and finally thorium to generate electricity. Nanotechnology works with materials at the nanometer scale, which is one billionth of a meter, to create new properties for medicine or electronics. In an ecosystem, energy flows in one direction from the sun to plants (producers) to animals (consumers) and then to decomposers, with only about 10% passing to the next level. Biodiversity hotspots are regions with many unique species that are under threat, like the Western Ghats in India. The Paris Agreement is a global climate treaty to limit global warming, while the Montreal Protocol is a separate treaty to protect the ozone layer by phasing out harmful chemicals. Water pollution is measured by BOD, or Biochemical Oxygen Demand, which tells how much oxygen microorganisms need to break down waste in water; higher BOD means more pollution. The Wildlife Protection Act (WPA) of 1972 is an Indian law that protects wild animals, birds, and plants by creating national parks and banning hunting.
